name: Global Ensemble Forecast Parser Nodes
description: Pure WASM parser flow nodes for a machine-learned global ensemble weather forecast source: parse_cloud_chunks joins the request-builder's per-chunk job JSON (one per Zarr v3 chunk of a cloud-cover array) with the matching hostcap/http-request responses POSITIONALLY (job k <-> response k), decodes each chunk through its declared codec chain (bytes float32/float16 in this build; a zstd stage reports codec-unsupported until a decoder is vendored), validates the byte length against the declared chunk shape, and emits one size-prefixed $WXF tile per chunk (own GRID, TILE_INDEX/TILE_COUNT over the declared global grid, VALUE_MIN/VALUE_MAX/MISSING_COUNT, licence class copied from the job) plus the storage.ingest_with_source meta (batch = sha256 of the concatenated chunk bodies, licence-bearing provenance). parse_cyclone_tracks turns the tropical-cyclone track CSV into one $TCT record per (storm, member) with points sorted by valid time, knots/hPa/nautical-mile source units converted exactly to m/s, Pa and km, wind radii at 34/50/64 kt by quadrant and the intensity category from maximum sustained wind; it emits the meta, the record stream and the raw CSV for archiving. Records are built with the spacedatastandards.org GENERATED C++ code. No capabilities: this node performs no I/O. Nothing about the upstream bucket layout is hardcoded — chunk shape, codecs, dimension order, dtype and grid arrive on the job JSON and are validated by size, because the store is allow-listed and its layout could not be verified anonymously.

sequentialJustification.detail: Both methods are single-pass transforms over the frames the flow hands them: parse_cloud_chunks decodes each chunk body once into one tile record, parse_cyclone_tracks walks the CSV rows once and groups them by storm and member. There is no shared mutable state, no worker pool and no fan-out inside the guest; the fan-out across chunks is the flow's, through the http connector node. This guest can never spawn a thread, so it compiles clang/wasi-sequential rather than claiming a wasi-threads contract it does not honour.

methods.description: Decodes N Zarr v3 chunk responses into N size-prefixed $WXF tile records plus one storage.ingest_with_source meta. Jobs and responses are paired BY POSITION (job k describes response k, exactly the order the request builder emitted them); differing counts are refused with job-response-count-mismatch rather than guessed, because a shifted pairing would label every later tile with the wrong array, lead or grid cell. A non-200 response fails the batch (fetch-failed); an undeclared codec fails it (codec-unsupported); a body whose length differs from product(chunk_shape) * itemsize fails it (chunk-size-mismatch). Padding beyond the declared global grid edge is dropped so an edge tile carries only real rows and columns. Both input ports are multi-stream by contract, so no batched-frame guard applies here.

methods.description: Decodes the tropical-cyclone track CSV (one row per storm x member x lead) into one size-prefixed $TCT record per (storm, member) with points in ascending valid time, exact unit conversions (1 kt = 1852/3600 m/s, 1 hPa = 100 Pa, 1 nmi = 1.852 km), quadrant wind radii at 34/50/64 kt (blank -> -1 not reported, 0 stays 0), intensity category from maximum sustained wind and the genesis/existing origin flag, plus the ingest meta (batch = sha256 of the CSV bytes) and the raw CSV for archiving. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE, not merely declared. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime - space_data_module_runtime_begin_node_invocation pops the node whole queue port-blind up to the drain budget (64) - so a node that read ordinal 0 of a port and returned would destroy every other frame it was handed there. A surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count. See graph task modules-guest-nodes-drop-batched-frames.
